title: Safety + Quality Pipeline Integration
brief: Wire handbook data into SafetyQualityHooks and quality pipeline engines. Use handbook-documented machine limits for program validation, alarm severity for safety escalation, positioning accuracy specs for metrology planning, and safety interlock documentation for lockout/tagout compliance.

units.title: Wire handbook machine limits into machineLimitGuard hook: validate G-code spindle speeds, feed rates, and axis positions against handbook-documented maximums instead of conservative generic limits
Wire handbook alarm severity into safety escalation: use OEM-classified alarm severity levels to determine operator notification urgency, automatic stop conditions, and required response actions
Wire handbook positioning accuracy and repeatability specs into MetrologyUncertaintyEngine: use machine-specific accuracy data for inspection planning and measurement uncertainty budgets
Build safety validation test suite: verify that programs exceeding handbook limits are caught, alarm escalation follows OEM severity, and metrology planning uses correct machine accuracy specs

exit_conditions: machineLimitGuard validates against handbook-documented limits when available, with correct fallback to generic limits
Alarm severity escalation uses OEM classifications from handbook data
MetrologyUncertaintyEngine uses handbook positioning accuracy specs for machines with ingested handbooks
Safety validation tests confirm all three integration points work correctly with handbook data present and absent
